interactions.summary: Students deepen the dream reading through father-killing and Star Wars analogies, and Jiang affirms that the dream is a turning-point warning that Dante has gone too far into Virgil's worldview and needs divine correction.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Student interpretations with Jiang expansion and confirmation.

speaker_notes.note: This appears to be a minimal student acknowledgment rather than a substantive turn.

claims.claim: Jiang accepts the reading that Dante's bond with Virgil has gone too far and treats the dream as a clarion call about dangerous overidentification with the father-guide.
Jiang uses the Star Wars father scene as an analogy for discovering oneself in the father one must symbolically overcome.
Jiang says Dante senses that Virgil's exposition of love is not right before he can fully explain why, and the universe responds by sending corrective dream images.
Jiang says that once one connects to the divine through love, the divine sends messages that steer the person even if the person remains partly corrupted.
A student adds that Beatrice asking Virgil to identify the siren suggests Virgilian possessive love is what beautifies the malformed woman by imagining possession.

signature_moments.moment: The universe is said to warn Dante directly: be aware of Virgil, because you are now Virgil.
signature_moments.source_phrase: be aware of Virgil. You are now Virgil
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It is the strongest statement of the dream's moral danger and of the guide-becoming-trap theme.

signature_moments.moment: Divine connection is figured as a steering mechanism that keeps sending messages even through corruption.
signature_moments.source_phrase: the divine will give you messages to show you the way
signature_moments.why_it_matters: Jiang's hermeneutics here depend on dream images as live guidance rather than static symbols.

chronology_notes.note: This packet sharpens Jiang's June 26 interpretation from Virgil-as-siren to a full warning that Dante is inheriting Virgil's distorted love unless divine images correct him.
